newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's PdVSA to cut 1997 investment $400 mln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's PdVSA to cut 1997 investment $400 mln.

text.p: Venezuelan state-owned oil company PdVSA will scale back planned 1997 investment by $400 million in response to IMF requests to curb inflationary pressures in the wider economy, government and PdVSA sources told Reuters.
However "the adjustment will not affect plans to increase production, at least not for the coming year," said one industry source who asked not to be named.

PdVSA has planned to boost current production by 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) from current levels of around three million barrels per day bpd through investments over ten years of some $6.5 billion annually.
Further cuts in 1997 spending of some $600 million will also be made by reducing operating costs and boosting efficiency, the sources said, when PdVSA's 1997 budget is finalized December 27.
"The cuts have been made to curb domestic aggregate demand and consequent inflationary pressures," the source said.

A recent IMF mission said Venezuela would have to deepen fiscal reforms and cut spending if it was to hit inflation targets. This year is expected to close with 100 percent inflation, falling to between 25 and 35 percent in 1997.
